task.description: WF-03 Step 4b hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's decision to commit NO new test for ISS-0446, running a widened-timing analog as one-off verification instead. Verify independently: (1) is the 'structurally impossible to regression-test' claim true -- try to construct a reliable, fast, deterministic test myself; (2) are the reported failure numbers real -- re-run the analog with my own script; (3) is a cheap non-timing guard warranted given the ISS-0378/ISS-0404/ISS-0413 precedent; (4) does test/specs/ISS-0446.md honestly represent the evidence; (5) is the 8-file finding correctly scoped out.

result.summary:
VERDICT: FAIL. TEST-DESIGNER's central load-bearing claim -- that the race is structurally impossible to reproduce reliably except under concurrent (async:true, many-sibling) contention, and therefore no committed regression test is achievable -- is WRONG, and I constructed a working counterexample myself. Items 2, 4 (partially), and 5 check out; item 1 does not, and item 3's conclusion (no cheap guard in scope) survives but its reasoning needs updating once item 1's finding lands.

=== ITEM 1: THE 'STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE' CLAIM IS FALSE ===

Built my own scripts (not reused from TEST-DESIGNER, written independently in scratch/tdv-iss0446/, deleted after use). Reproduced their OLD-shape (Supervisor.start_link/2 unnamed + on_exit(fn -> if Process.alive?(sup_pid), do: Supervisor.stop(sup_pid) end), child terminate/2 sleeps 5ms) and NEW-shape (fetch_test_supervisor/0 + start_supervised!/1, no on_exit) constructions, and additionally tested configurations TEST-DESIGNER's spec does not report trying.

First, confirmed their async:true/80-siblings result independently: OLD shape, 4 runs of 80 async:true cases -> MY OWN MEASURED COUNTS: 10/80, 10/80, 11/80, 14/80 failures (same order of magnitude as their reported 6/80,2/80,8/80,9/80; mine ran hotter, consistent with ordinary machine-load variance, not a discrepancy). NEW shape, 5 runs of 80 async:true cases -> 0/80 every time (400/400 clean), exact match to their reported 400/400.

Then tested the claim that follows from this -- that async:true concurrency specifically is the necessary ingredient and no sequential/async:false construction can reproduce it. THIS IS WHERE THE SPEC IS WRONG. I ran the identical OLD-shape pattern as async:false (fully sequential) with 150 test cases in one module: 25/150, 19/150, 12/150 failures across 3 runs -- reproducing the exact same stacktrace (GenServer.stop/3 -> :sys.terminate exited shutdown, and the :noproc variant) verified by inspecting the actual failure detail. I re-ran forcing max_cases:1 explicitly (eliminating any doubt that ExUnit was silently running siblings concurrently): 34/150 failures, same stacktrace. I then found the minimal reliable, FAST shape: 20 sequential async:false test cases at Process.sleep(5), real wall-clock time under 1.3 seconds per run -- 5/5 runs each produced 2-4 failures (never zero). At N=10 it was less reliable (4/6 runs nonzero) but N=20 was 5/5 nonzero across every run I tried.

I also isolated WHY: a control probe looping the same check-then-act pattern 20 times INSIDE ONE test via try/catch :exit (bypassing ExUnit's on_exit-runner mechanism entirely) produced 0/20 crashes. This shows the race is not merely 'BEAM scheduler doing many start/stop cycles fast' -- it specifically requires ExUnit's own on_exit callback running in a separate on_exit-runner process, asynchronously relative to whatever happens next, and it fires reliably once enough such on_exit cycles run back-to-back in the same BEAM VM, WITH OR WITHOUT async:true. TEST-DESIGNER attributed the necessary ingredient to 'concurrent (async:true) scheduler contention among siblings'; the real necessary ingredient is 'enough on_exit-driven start/stop cycles in the same VM run,' which async:false sequential execution supplies just as well once N is large enough (about 20+ in my measurements). Their claim that async:false at sleep values 1-50ms across 100+ runs reproduced ZERO failures does not match what I found -- I did not run their exact script, but the same mechanism, same sleep value, same on_exit-based construction, under async:false, reproduced it reliably at N=20 and above.

CONSEQUENCE: a reliable, fast (<2s), deterministic-enough (nonzero every run tested) regression test IS constructible: an async:false describe block of ~20-30 test cases using the exact old on_exit(fn -> if Process.alive?(pid), do: Supervisor.stop(pid) end) shape with a child whose terminate/2 does deliberate work (Process.sleep(5) suffices), asserted to have zero on_exit-teardown-crash failures when run against the FIXED (start_supervised!-based) code, would have caught a reintroduction of the check-then-act pattern -- because it reliably fails (2-4/20 every run I measured) against the OLD pattern. This directly falsifies the spec's basis for not committing anything: the choice was framed as 'commit a flaky/expensive async:true 80-case file' vs 'commit nothing,' when a cheaper, smaller, sequential, near-instant option that TEST-DESIGNER did not try was available and works.

=== ITEM 2: REPORTED NUMBERS ARE REAL ===
Independently confirmed both the OLD-shape failure pattern (mechanism, stacktrace, and rough failure rate under async:true) and the NEW-shape 400/400 clean result, using my own scripts. No numbers fabricated. This part of the spec is trustworthy.

=== ITEM 3: CHEAP NON-TIMING GUARD ===
Re-confirmed the 8-file grep finding exactly (grep -rn 'on_exit.*Process.alive?' test/ -> 8 real hits across 5 files, matching TEST-DESIGNER's citations line-for-line). Reviewed ISS-0378/ISS-0404/ISS-0413: that precedent is specifically about EVERGREEN-PROPERTY-VIA-GIT-DIFF/GIT-HISTORY tests being deleted for depending on git ref/SHA resolution at test-run time (shallow checkouts, squash-merges) -- a different fragility class from a grep-over-test-source lint gate, which depends on nothing but the checked-out tree. The precedent does not directly counsel against a static grep-based lint gate the way it would against a git-diff-based one. That said, given Item 1's finding, a suite-wide grep lint gate is now a WEAKER second choice, not the main gap: the actual gap is that a working, cheap, timing-based regression test for THIS file was achievable and not built. TEST-DESIGNER's scope reasoning for not expanding the grep-gate suite-wide (out of ISS-0446's own affected_files) is sound and I do not fault that scoping decision on its own.

=== ITEM 4: SPEC HONESTY ===
Mostly honest. The async-only caveat is stated plainly and repeatedly, not buried, and the 'mechanism evidence, not proof of absence' framing is appropriately hedged and matches what the evidence actually supports for the NEW-shape/OLD-shape comparison itself. HOWEVER: the spec's causal attribution -- 'Only concurrent (async:true) scheduling... reproduces the window' and 'early attempts at async:false... reproduced zero failures across 10+80+ runs' -- is a factual claim I could not reproduce and could actively falsify with the same mechanism at N=20+. This is not a framing/emphasis problem, it is an incorrect mechanistic claim that the entire non-commit decision rests on. It should be corrected, not merely re-worded.

=== ITEM 5: 8-FILE FINDING SCOPE ===
Correctly scoped OUT of this run on its own terms (real finding, accurately counted, legitimately suite-wide, properly deferred to a follow-up issue per Unblock-Everything's scope boundary). No change needed here regardless of the Item 1 outcome.

=== CLEANUP ===
All probe scripts lived under scratch/tdv-iss0446/ and were deleted after use. git status --porcelain lib/ test/ scratch/ (from repo root) returned EMPTY. Re-ran the real modified test file: mix test test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs -> 'Result: 42 passed' (37.9s, includes DB setup/teardown), 0 failures, confirming no residue and the fix itself remains green throughout my probing.

=== WHY THIS IS A FAIL, NOT A MINOR NOTE ===
This is not a case of 'the argument is well-written but I'll rubber-stamp it' nor 'reflexively demanding a test where none is warranted.' The specific empirical claim that grounds the entire non-commit decision (reason #1 in the spec: 'the analog only reproduces reliably under concurrent... scheduler contention... a single, isolated, async:false instance... is not reliably flaky') is factually wrong, and a cheap, fast, reliable alternative exists that was never tried. Per this role's mandate ('FAIL immediately and completely on any single check failing') and the 'don't rubber-stamp a well-written argument' instruction, this must FAIL and go back to TEST-DESIGNER.

issues.title: TEST-DESIGNER's test/specs/ISS-0446.md misattributes the race's necessary condition to async:true concurrency; a fast, reliable async:false sequential test reproduces it
issues.description: The spec's central non-commit justification (reason 1) claims the race 'only reproduces reliably under concurrent (async:true) scheduler contention' and that async:false at sleep values 1-50ms reproduced zero failures across 100+ runs. TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently constructed an async:false, max_cases:1, single-BEAM-process test module with 20 sequential test cases of the identical old check-then-act shape (Process.sleep(5) in terminate/2) and reproduced the identical failure (same GenServer.stop/:sys.terminate/shutdown stacktrace, and the :noproc variant) in 5/5 runs, 2-4/20 failures each run, total wall time under 1.3s per run. The true necessary condition is 'enough on_exit-driven supervisor start/stop cycles running back-to-back in one BEAM VM' (confirmed by a control probe: looping the same pattern via try/catch inside ONE test, bypassing ExUnit's on_exit-runner process, produced 0/20 crashes) -- async:true is a sufficient but not necessary way to supply that condition; a moderately-sized async:false describe block supplies it just as reliably. This means a committable regression test achievable in well under 2 seconds of CI time was available and not built, directly undermining the spec's stated cost/benefit tradeoff for not committing anything.

result.next_action: Route back to TEST-DESIGNER (rework) with this finding. Direction for rework, not prescribed as the only path but concretely actionable: build and commit a small (~20-30 case), async:false, fast (<2s) regression test module using the exact deleted old on_exit(fn -> if Process.alive?(pid), do: Supervisor.stop(pid) end) shape against a deliberately-slow (Process.sleep 5ms+) supervised child, asserting it against the SHIPPED fixed code path has zero on_exit-teardown-crash failures across N runs -- since the fixed code (fetch_test_supervisor!/start_supervised!) has no on_exit at all and no Process.alive? check anywhere in its teardown path, this test would pass reliably against the fix and (per my own 5/5 measurement) would have failed reliably against the deleted old pattern, making it a genuine, cheap, fast discriminating regression test rather than a rejected 80-case async:true flake risk. Re-verify the async:false/N=20+ mechanism once more before committing (my measurement is solid but TEST-DESIGNER should reproduce it independently rather than take my numbers on faith, per this project's own re-derive-don't-inherit rule). If TEST-DESIGNER still concludes no test should be committed after trying this shape, that conclusion must be re-argued against this specific counterexample, not the async:true-only framing already shown wrong.
